title: "14. Age-structured transmission with a contact matrix"

## Overview

Age-structured models use a contact matrix `C`, with `C[i, j]` the daily number of contacts
an individual in group `i` has with group `j`, and a per-contact transmission probability
`q`. With `n` groups the next-generation matrix is `n × n` and irreducible, so there is no
closed form beyond `n = 2`; everything is numeric. This vignette builds a six-group SEIR
model with a synthetic but realistically shaped contact matrix (assortative mixing with a
school-age peak), computes `R₀`, the Perron vector (which age groups the growing epidemic
concentrates in), the reproductive values, elasticities with respect to each contact
block, and the effect of vaccinating one age group.

## The model

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics, LinearAlgebra
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

n = 6
groups = ["0-4", "5-14", "15-24", "25-44", "45-64", "65+"]
@parameters q σ γ C[1:n, 1:n] N[1:n]
@variables S(t)[1:n] E(t)[1:n] I(t)[1:n] R(t)[1:n]
Cm, Nv, Sv, Ev, Iv, Rv = collect(C), collect(N), collect(S), collect(E), collect(I), collect(R)
λ = [q * sum(Cm[i, j] * Iv[j] / Nv[j] for j in 1:n) for i in 1:n]
eqs = vcat([D(Sv[i]) ~ -λ[i] * Sv[i] for i in 1:n],
           [D(Ev[i]) ~ λ[i] * Sv[i] - σ * Ev[i] for i in 1:n],
           [D(Iv[i]) ~ σ * Ev[i] - γ * Iv[i] for i in 1:n],
           [D(Rv[i]) ~ γ * Iv[i] for i in 1:n])
age = complete(System(eqs, t; name = :age))
ngm = next_generation_matrix(age, vcat(Ev, Iv); equilibrium = Dict(Sv[i] => Nv[i] for i in 1:n))
size(ngm.K), length(states_at_infection(ngm))
```

Symbolically, `K[i, j] = q C[i, j] (Nᵢ/Nⱼ) / γ` (the exposed states are the
states-at-infection; the `σ` cancels because everyone exposed becomes infectious):

```{julia}
ngm.K[1, 2]
```

## Numbers

```{julia}
contacts = [ 7.0 3.0 1.5 3.0 1.0 0.5;
             2.5 12.0 3.0 3.5 1.5 0.5;
             1.0 2.5 9.0 4.0 2.0 0.5;
             1.5 2.0 3.0 7.0 3.0 1.0;
             0.5 1.0 1.5 3.0 5.0 1.5;
             0.3 0.4 0.5 1.5 2.0 3.0 ]
sizes = [280.0, 600.0, 640.0, 1400.0, 1300.0, 900.0]   # thousands
vals = Dict{Any, Any}(Cm[i, j] => contacts[i, j] for i in 1:n, j in 1:n)
for i in 1:n
    vals[Nv[i]] = sizes[i]
end
vals[q] = 0.05
vals[σ] = 0.25
vals[γ] = 0.2
num = evaluate(ngm, vals)
R0 = basic_reproduction_number(num)
```

The same number from the reciprocity-corrected contact matrix directly:

```{julia}
Kdirect = [0.05 * contacts[i, j] * sizes[i] / sizes[j] / 0.2 for i in 1:n, j in 1:n]
maximum(abs, eigvals(Kdirect))
```

## Who drives transmission?

The right Perron vector `u` is the age distribution of new infections in the exponential
phase; the left vector `v` holds reproductive values, the relative contribution of an
infection in each group to future growth:

```{julia}
u, v = perron_vectors(num)
[groups round.(u; digits = 3) round.(v; digits = 3)]
```

Elasticities of `R₀` with respect to each contact block, aggregated by the group making the
contact, show where interventions have leverage. Because the closed form does not exist we
differentiate numerically through the numeric eigenvalue with finite differences:

```{julia}
function elasticity_numeric(vals, θ; h = 1e-6)
    v₊ = copy(vals); v₊[θ] = vals[θ] * (1 + h)
    v₋ = copy(vals); v₋[θ] = vals[θ] * (1 - h)
    (basic_reproduction_number(ngm, v₊) - basic_reproduction_number(ngm, v₋)) / (2h * R0)
end
by_group = [sum(elasticity_numeric(vals, Cm[i, j]) for j in 1:n) for i in 1:n]
[groups round.(by_group; digits = 3)]
```

## Vaccinating one group

Vaccinating a fraction `vᵢ` of group `i` (all-or-nothing protection) removes that fraction
of `Sᵢ` from the infection-free state, scaling row `i` of `K` by `1 - vᵢ`. The type
reproduction number of group `i` tells us whether vaccinating that group alone can bring
`R₀` below one, and what coverage is needed:

```{julia}
Tg = [try type_reproduction_number(num, i) catch; NaN end for i in 1:n]
[groups round.(Tg; digits = 2) round.(1 .- 1 ./ Tg; digits = 2)]
```

Groups with `NaN` cannot be targeted alone: the rest of the population sustains
transmission without them. For a group that can, the critical coverage `1 - 1/Tᵢ` brings
`R₀` to exactly one:

```{julia}
i = findfirst(x -> !isnan(x) && x > 1, Tg)
if i !== nothing
    vals_v = copy(vals)
    @parameters v
    ngm_v = next_generation_matrix(age, vcat(Ev, Iv);
                                   equilibrium = merge(Dict(Sv[k] => Nv[k] for k in 1:n), Dict(Sv[i] => (1 - v) * Nv[i])))
    vals_v[v] = 1 - 1 / Tg[i]
    (groups[i], basic_reproduction_number(ngm_v, vals_v))
end
```
